name: Volcanic & aviation ash
summary: No red aviation codes, VEI 4+ eruptions or ash-related airspace closures found as of 12 Nov
state: Searches on 12 Nov found no red aviation colour code, no VEI 4+ eruption and no major ash-related airspace closure. Mayon in the Philippines has been at Alert Level 3 since an explosive eruption on 30 Oct, a local hazard rather than one disrupting major air routes. The Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program's lists of current eruptions and weekly activity show no new large eruption, so the signal stays Normal.
for_you: No widespread flight disruption from volcanic ash is expected. Travellers to areas near active volcanoes, such as Albay in the Philippines, should follow local authority and FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Normal: no aviation colour code red and no large eruption found as of 12 Nov

why: Major eruptions ground flights (Iceland 2010) and can cool the climate for years.
drivers: Volcanic unrest; impact depends on ash plume height and jet-stream direction.

rubric.alert: Major airspace closures from ash, or a VEI 4+ eruption.
rubric.watch: Aviation colour code orange/red at a volcano near major air routes, or a large eruption.
rubric.normal: No aviation colour code red; no large eruptions.
